list.name: Changes
list.comment:
Fix jffi add to handle binary files (Android images, etc.)
Critical fix: jffi add crashed on platforms with binary files
Problem: - jffi add android failed with 'stream did not contain valid UTF-8' - copy_dir_with_render() used fs::read_to_string() on ALL files - Android templates have binary files (PNG images, etc.) - Reading binary as UTF-8 text causes error
Root cause: - jffi new had proper binary file handling (try text, fallback to copy) - jffi add was missing this fallback logic - Only worked for platforms with text-only files (iOS, macOS, Windows)
Solution: - Match jffi new's implementation - Try fs::read_to_string() first (for template rendering) - On UTF-8 error, fall back to fs::copy() (binary files) - Binary files copied as-is without template rendering
Now works for all platforms: ✅ iOS (text files only) ✅ macOS (text files only) ✅ Windows (text files only) ✅ Android (has PNG images, gradle binaries, etc.) ✅ Web (may have binary assets) ✅ Linux (may have binary assets)

- Remove todo/counter template options (marked as coming soon) - Simplify all platform UIs (iOS, macOS, Android, Windows, Linux, Web) to use only core.greeting() with refresh button - Block todo/counter selection from CLI and interactive UI - All platforms now generate consistent hello world app

- Remove todo/counter template options (marked as coming soon) - Simplify all platform UIs (iOS, macOS, Android, Windows, Linux, Web) to use only core.greeting() with refresh button - Block todo/counter selection from CLI and interactive UI - All platforms now generate consistent hello world app

Auto-detect host architecture for Windows dev hot reload
Smart default for first build:
Before: - First hot reload would pick random architecture - Or default to x64 regardless of host CPU - ARM64 users would get wrong build
After: - Detects host CPU via PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE env var - Uses host architecture as default for first build - Subsequent builds use most recently built platform - Shows 'Detected host architecture: x64' on first build
Implementation: - detect_host_windows_architecture() - reads env var - Maps AMD64→x64, x86→x86, ARM64→ARM64 - detect_active_windows_platform() falls back to host arch - Works for both jffi dev and jffi run
Benefits: - Faster first build (only 1 arch instead of 3) - Correct architecture by default - Works on x64, x86, and ARM64 Windows machines - Consistent with run command behavior
Example output (first build): '→ Detected host architecture: x64' '→ Building Rust for x64 only...'
Example output (subsequent builds): '→ Building Rust for x64 only...' (uses last built)

Auto-detect host architecture for Windows builds - only build all with --deploy
Major optimization for Windows development workflow:
Before: - jffi build --platform windows: builds x86, x64, ARM64 (slow) - jffi dev: detects active platform from bin/ folder - First build always builds all 3 architectures
After: - jffi build --platform windows: builds only host architecture (3x faster) - jffi build --platform windows --deploy: builds all architectures - jffi dev: uses host architecture as default for first build - jffi run: uses host architecture (fast)
Implementation: - Added --deploy flag to build command - detect_host_windows_architecture() reads PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE - build_windows_host_arch() builds only detected architecture - build_windows_all_archs() builds all (for deployment) - build_windows_archs() shared implementation - detect_active_windows_platform() falls back to host arch
Benefits: - Much faster development builds (1 arch instead of 3) - Correct architecture by default (no more ARM64 on x64 machines) - Explicit --deploy flag for distribution builds - Consistent with dev command behavior - Works on x64, x86, and ARM64 Windows machines
Example usage: - Development: jffi build --platform windows (builds x64 only on x64 machine) - Deployment: jffi build --platform windows --deploy (builds all 3) - Hot reload: jffi dev --platform windows (auto-detects x64) - Run: jffi run --platform windows (auto-detects x64)
